correctness.rationale: The balanced q-adic construction has M_l comparable to q^{(1-alpha)l}, two-sided boundary-neighborhood size r^alpha, and matching translation and lattice symmetric-difference lower bounds at odd levels. In the gamma<eta regime a single nonzero Fourier coefficient of a spectral box converts the lattice lower bound directly through the exact trace-defect identity. In the gamma>eta regime Parseval converts the spectral translation lower bound into the weighted Fourier sum for an interval lattice, and axial tensorization supplies the factor N^{d-1}. The product boundary hypotheses and all exponent comparisons were checked separately.

originality.rationale: Mayeli arXiv:2609.12226v1 explicitly leaves both off-critical powers open in Remark 9.4 and presents alternating-gap Cantor examples only as numerical evidence. Searches of trace-defect sharpness, discrete Fourier concentration, fractional translation and Minkowski regularity, Cantor/Moran examples, source identifiers, and current SCOPE records found no proof of the all-parameter lower bounds. Residual risk remains from a very recent or differently indexed contemporaneous observation.

value.rationale: The theorem settles both off-critical sharpness questions for every dimension and every unequal pair of exponents, and identifies the smaller regularity exponent as sufficient by allowing the other side to remain smooth. It also supplies an explicit all-fractional-exponent construction rather than only isolated self-similar parameters.
